Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:10:1.hebrew: כשנתחייב שבועה בב"ד - דכיון דתבעו בעדים לקיים דברי ב"ד ולא אבה, אינו נאמן לומר עוד קיימתי אחרי כן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:10:1.english: When he was obligated [to take] an oath in court - For since [the claimant] demanded of him before witnesses to fulfill the words of the court, and he did not want [to], he is no longer believed to say afterward, "I fulfilled [it]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:10:2.hebrew: אבל חייב עצמו שבועה - שאמר לו אשבע לך, ותבעו בעדים ולא אבה, ואחר כך אמר נשבעתי — נאמן, ואע"ג דקמי עדים דחייה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:10:2.english: But [if] he obligated himself [to take] an oath - [That is,] where he said to him, "I will swear to you," and [the other] demanded [it of] him before witnesses and he did not consent, and afterward he said, "I swore" — he is believed, even though before witnesses he put him off.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:10:3.hebrew: עביד איניש דמקרי ואמר - לא אעשה מה שלא חייבוני ב"ד אלא אני בעצמי, ואין זו סרבנות וחרטה אלא דחייה בעלמא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:10:3.english: A person is prone to say incidentally - "I will not do what the court did not obligate me [to do], only [what] I myself [obligated myself]," and this is not stubbornness and retraction, rather mere deferral.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:12:1.english: And its date is written in it on that same day - [Meaning] that it was written on the day it was found.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:14:1.hebrew: שכבר נמחל שעבודו - משפרע מלוה ראשונה, ועל האחרונה לא נכתב, והויא לה מלוה על פה, וטורף לקוחות שלא כדין, דאין מלוה על פה גובה מן הלקוחות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:14:1.english: As its lien is already forgiven - Once he repaid the first loan, and [the note] was not written for the latter [loan], it is [considered] a verbal loan, and he seizes [property from] buyers unlawfully, since a verbal loan does not collect from buyers.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:15:1.hebrew: אימת - דפרעיה אימתי, וחזר ולוה אימתי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:15:1.english: When - [That is,] when did he repay him, and when did he borrow again?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:15:2.english: If we say [it was] the next day - and not on the day that it was written.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:15:3.hebrew: וליומא חרא - שתי תיבות הן, וליום אחריו, וקיצור סופרים הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:15:3.english: And to another day [ul'yoma chara] - They are two words, [meaning] "and to the day after it," and it is a scribal contraction.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:15:4.hebrew: תיפוק ליה - דאפילו נכתב על מלוה זו אחרונה, וכתוב בו יום מוקדם כזה, הוה ליה השטר מוקדם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:15:4.english: Let it be derived - For even if it was written for this latter loan, and an earlier date like this is written in it, the document is antedated.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:17:1.hebrew: דלא שכיחי [אינשי] דפרעי [ביומיה] קאמינא - הלכך, לא חיישינן למידי דלא שכיח, ואי אתרמי, הוצרכו לומר דאין חוזר ולוה בו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:17:1.english: I said that [people] do not commonly repay [on the same day] - Therefore, we do not concern ourselves with something that is uncommon; and if it happens [that one repays on the same day], [the Sages] needed to state that one may not borrow again with it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:18:1.hebrew: רב כהנא אמר - הא דא"ר יוחנן, יחזיר לבעלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:18:1.english: Rav Kahana says - [This refers to] that which Rabbi Yochanan said, "He shall return [it] to the owner."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:18:2.english: When [the] liable party admits - That he has not paid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:19:1.english: The Sages will hear - that its lien was waived.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:19:2.hebrew: ומפסדי לי - למטרף לקוחות, משום דשטרי חוב המוקדמין פסולין, דכיון דהאי דאוקמא הכי לית ליה "עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו", אף זה מן המוקדמין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:19:2.english: And will cause me to lose - [the right] to seize [property from] purchasers, because predated promissory notes are invalid, for since this [sage] who established it thus does not hold [that] "its witnesses, by their signatures, acquire for him," this [note] too is [considered] among the predated [notes].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:1:1.english: And he said - After some time.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:1:2.english: I repaid - By order of the court.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:1:3.english: Deemed credible - And [this is] with a heset oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:1:4.hebrew: בא מלוה - לפנינו לכתוב לו אדרכתא עליו, אין כותבין ונותנין לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:1:4.english: [If] a creditor comes - before us to write for him an authorization [*adrakhta*] against him, we do not write [it] and give [it] to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:23:1.hebrew: מינח ניחא ליה - ברמאות, ותלי נפשיה בספיקא, ואמר: דלמא לא שמעי ואיכא רווחא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:23:1.english: It is satisfactory to him - [to engage] in deception, and he places himself in [a position of] uncertainty, and says [to himself]: Perhaps they will not hear [about it], and there will be a benefit.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:23:2.hebrew: מאי איכא דטריף לקוחות - מה טרפא יש בזה שלא יהא בשטר שיחזור ויכתוב לו? והלא שניהם ביום אחד? הלכך, בשטר שנמחל שעבודו לא שביק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:23:2.english: What is there [that] he repossesses [from] purchasers - What [power of] repossession is there in this [note] that would not be in a [new] note that he would go back and write for him? Are not both of them [dated] on the same day? Therefore, he does not allow [it] with a note whose lien was forgiven.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:24:1.hebrew: הטוען אחר מעשה ב"ד - דבר שהוא תנאי ב"ד, כגון כתובה ומזון האשה והבנות; הטוען ואמר "פרעתי" שלא בעדים, לא אמר כלום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:24:1.english: One who claims [to have paid] after an enactment of the court - [That is,] something that is a stipulation of the court, such as a ketubah and the sustenance of the wife and the daughters — one who claims and says, "I have paid," without witnesses, has said nothing.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:2:1.hebrew: אינו נאמן - לישבע, אלא שכנגדו נשבע ונוטל, דכיון דתחילתו הוצרך לתובעו לדין, אין דרכו למהר לפרוע עד שיפסקו דינו פסק גמור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:2:1.english: He is not deemed credible - to take an oath; rather, his opponent takes an oath and collects, for since at the outset [the creditor] had to summon him to court, it is not his way to hasten to repay until they issue a final verdict in his case.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:3:1.hebrew: ואמר פרעתי - לאחר זמן ע"פ ב"ד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:3:1.english: And he said, "I repaid" - After some time, by order of the court.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:4:1.hebrew: והעדים מעידים אותו שלא פרע - "בפנינו תבעו לפרוע לו ע"פ ב"ד ולא פרעו." הואיל ובפניהם העיז לעבור ע"פ ב"ד, אינו נאמן שוב לומר "פרעתיו" שלא בעדים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:4:1.english: And the witnesses testify concerning him that he did not repay - [The witnesses testify:] "In our presence he demanded of him to pay him by order of the court, and he did not pay him." Since in their presence he was brazen [enough] to defy the order of the court, he is no longer believed to say, "I repaid him," without witnesses.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:4:2.hebrew: הוחזק כפרן לאותו ממון - שאין נאמן עוד עליו לומר החזרתי ופרעתי, עד שיפרע בעדים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:4:2.english: He has assumed the presumptive status of a denier with regard to that money - For he is no longer believed regarding it to say, "I returned [it] and paid," until he pays before witnesses.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:5:1.hebrew: לא הוחזק כפרן - ונשבע שפרעו, ואע"פ שלא פרעו מיד כשתבעו בפני עדים, ואין זה מעיז ב"ד, דכיון דלא פסקו לו פסק גמור, נשמט ממנו, סבר כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:5:1.english: He does not assume the presumptive status of one who denies [his debts] - And he takes an oath that he repaid him, even though he did not repay him immediately when [the creditor] demanded [payment] from him in the presence of witnesses; and this is not [considered] acting brazenly [toward] the court, for since they did not issue a final verdict for him, he evaded him, thinking, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:8:2.english: He is presumed a denier with regard to that cloak - [and remains so] until he pays.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:9:1.hebrew: הוחזק כפרן לאותה שבועה - לומר נשבעתי, עד שישבע בפנינו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 17a:9:1.english: He is established as a denier with regard to that oath - [He is not believed] to say, "I swore," until he swears before us.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 17a:18:1.hebrew: רב כהנא אמר כשחייב מודה - תימה, א"כ למה נקט הנפק במילתא דר' יוחנן? וי"ל דנקטיה משום דיוקא: דאי אין כתוב בו ביום — אפילו כתוב בו הנפק, דודאי לוה — לא יחזיר, דחיישינן לקנוניא או לפשיטי דספרא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 17a:18:1.english: Rav Kahana says: When the liable party admits - It is astonishing: if so, why did he mention validation [henpek] in Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement? And one can say that he mentioned it because of the inference: that if it is not dated that same day — even if validation is written in it, where he certainly borrowed — he may not return [it], because we are concerned about collusion or about the scribe's fees.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 17a:24:1.hebrew: הטוען אחר מעשה ב"ד לא אמר כלום - אינו נאמן לומר "פרעתי". מעשה ב"ד קרי כל דבר שחייב לה אפי' לא כתב, כגון מנה ומאתים, ומזון האשה והבנות לאחר מותו. וא"ת: למה כותבין כתובה, כיון דבלאו כתובה נמי אין נאמן לומר "פרעתי"? וי"ל: משום תוספת, אבל מנה ומאתים גבייה בלא כתובה. ותוספת — נראה דאפי' אית לה סהדי דהתנה לה, נאמן לומר "פרעתי". ואין ראיה מכלתי' דר' שבתאי, דהוה מהימן לומר "פרעתי" אי לאו דהוחזק כפרן; דר' שבתאי ערב היה, אבל בעל שמא לא היה נאמן. ואין ראיה נמי מדתני לעיל (בבא מציעא דף ז:): "מצא כתובה לא יחזיר" — ומשמע דלא יחזיר משום תוספת, שהיה נאמן לומר "פרעתי" — דלגבי מנה ומאתים נמי מפסיד: דהא נאמן לומר "פרעתי מנה" מגו דאי בעי אמר "אלמנה נשאתיך", אם אין לה עדי הינומא; או אם אין לה עדי קדושין, נאמן לומר "פרעתי הכל" במגו דאי בעי אמר "אין את אשתי". וא"ת: דבפרק אלמנה ניזונית (כתובות דף צו. ושם ד"ה יתומים) בעי רבי יוחנן: היא אמרה "לא נתנו מזונות" ויתומים אמרו "נתננו", על מי להביא ראיה? והא אית ליה הכא דלא אמר כלום! וי"ל: דהתם מיירי במזונות דלשעבר, ולא בלהבא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 17a:24:1.english: One who claims [to have paid] after a court enactment has said nothing - He is not believed to say, "I paid." A "court enactment" refers to anything he is obligated [to pay] her even if he did not write [it in a marriage contract], such as the maneh [one hundred zuz] and matayim [two hundred zuz], and the sustenance of the wife and the daughters after his death. And if you ask: Why do we write a ketubah, since even without a ketubah he is not believed to say, "I paid"? One can answer: Because of the tosefet [the additional sum], whereas maneh and matayim she collects without a ketubah. And [regarding] tosefet — it appears that even if she has witnesses that he stipulated [it] for her, he is believed to say, "I paid." And there is no proof from [the case of] Rabbi Shabtai's daughter-in-law, where he would have been believed to say, "I paid" had he not been established as a liar — for Rabbi Shabtai was a guarantor, whereas a husband perhaps would not be believed. And there is also no proof from what is taught above (Bava Metzia 7b): "If one found a ketubah, he should not return [it]" — which implies he should not return [it] because of the tosefet, where he would be believed to say, "I paid" — because regarding maneh and matayim as well, [she] loses out: for he is believed to say, "I paid a maneh," with a migo [the legal principle that one is believed because he could have made a more advantageous claim] that if he wanted, he could say, "I married you as a widow," if she does not have witnesses of a hinuma [bridal veil]; or if she does not have witnesses of betrothal, he is believed to say, "I paid everything," with a migo that if he wanted, he could say, "You are not my wife." And if you ask: In the chapter Almanah Nizonet (Ketubot 96a, and there s.v. Yetomim), Rabbi Yoḥanan asks: [If] she says, "They did not give [me] sustenance," and the orphans say, "We gave [it]," upon whom is it to bring proof? But he holds here that [one who claims against a court enactment] has said nothing! One can answer: There it is speaking of past sustenance, and not future [sustenance].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 17a:2:1.hebrew: חייב אתה ליתן לו - הכא משמע ד"חייב אתה ליתן לו" לא הוי פסק דין גמור, כי אם "צא ותן לו", וכן משמע במרובה (ב"ק דף סט. ושם). וקשה, דבפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ו: ושם) אמרינן: ה"ד גמר דין? "פלוני אתה חייב, פלוני אתה זכאי". וי"ל, דהתם מקרי גמר דין לענין שאסור לבצוע, לפי שיודע להיכן הדין נוטה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 17a:2:1.english: You are liable to give him - Here it is implied that "You are liable to give him" is not a complete final verdict, but rather "Go and give [it] to him" [is], and so it is implied in [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 69a, and there). And this is difficult, for in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (6b, and there) we say: What is a final verdict? "So-and-so, you are liable; so-and-so, you are exempt." And one can answer that there it is called a final verdict with respect to [the rule] that it is forbidden to mediate a compromise, because one knows which way the judgment is leaning.
